Paul: Quick clarifying Q from the all-hands: when you say the moat is serving not models, what's the one-sentence we should use on partner calls?

Elena (CEO): Say: "Redwood turns model capability into predictable product outcomes: consistent latency, transparent unit costs, and deployment flexibility." Short and outcome-focused.

Zoe (Marketing): Can we publish a public-friendly stat? Or keep numbers internal?

Maya (VP Product): Internally we standardize p50/p95/p99 by workload. Publicly, use conservative, contextual numbers with the workload noted.

Ravi (CTO): Tech add: highlight levers (batching, KV/prefix cache, quant profiles) that compound savings. Those are why serving matters.

Paul: For objections like "we can self-host cheaper", can we get a 1-line rebuttal?

Elena (CEO): "Self-hosting often hides ops and tuning costs; we deliver predictable economics and guardrails so features ship and stay healthy."

Maya (VP Product): Action items: Zoe drafts a short public blurb by Wed, Ravi to give a 1-slide tech appendix by Tue, and Paul will pilot the one-line rebuttal this week.

all-hands-bot: Notes saved. Recording and slides will be posted to #all-hands-resources.
